item.title: Labyrinth: A 40th Anniversary Screening
item.description: On Monday, January 12th and Tuesday, January 13th, Light House Cinema was alive with 1980s glam rock music and insane feats of puppetry that is Labyrinth (Jim Henson, 1986). It has been 40 years since the film was first released, but it was clear from the crowds of parents with children in the theatre that its magic will be dutifully passed on to generations to come. item.title: Irish Legacies: Carmilla on the Heidelberg Stage
item.description: In 1872 Trinity alumni Sheridan Le Fanu publishes his career-defining novella Carmilla; a text which will come to revolutionize the way that we understand Gothic literature, female vampirism and queerness. 150 years later, its stage adaptation can be found on the doorstep of the “Romanischen Keller”, the home of one of Germany’s oldest English-speaking theatre groups. item.title: The Philosophy of Pluribus
item.description: Vince Gilligan, the showrunner of Breaking Bad and Better Call Saul, has made his foray into science fiction with Pluribus. His vision of the apocalypse is a galactic spam-email virus. A transmission from 600 lightyears away reaches a baffled coterie of astronomers, who promptly set about testing what appears to be the genetic code for a lysogenic virus. item.title: “This is the Place”: An Audio and Visual Installation in the Samuel Beckett Theatre
item.description: The University Times had the pleasure of sitting down with Rachel Holmes, a Senior Sophister (Drama Studies) student at Trinity College Dublin. The undertaking of her final year capstone project, entitled “This is the Place” is currently underway. item.title: Trinity Sailing Hosts Women at the Helm 2026
item.description: On February 7th, Trinity Sailing hosted 18 teams (108 people) for their Women at the Helm Event at Royal St George Yacht Club in Dún Laoghaire. The 2026 event follows the inaugural Women at the Helm 2025 event, which also aimed to promote inclusivity and empower female athletes. The event, which was open to college students and alumni, was in a 3v3 racing format, where each team had three women at the wheel. item.title: Trinity Sailing Secures Historic Win in Oxford Top Gun Invitational
item.description: On the 24th of January, Trinity Sailing, represented by students Sam Ledoux, Georgia Goodbody, Trevor Bolger, Conor Lynch, Harry Twomey, and Orla Gilroy, competed in the Oxford Top Gun Invitational. Trinity Sailing achieved first place for the first time ever and became the second Irish team to win, earning an invitation to return next year to defend their title. item.description: The phenomenon is predictable just as are the seasons. item.title: Motaz Azaiza Receives Law Soc’s Praeses Elit Award
item.description: On February 5th, Dublin University Law Society (Law Soc) presented the Praeses Elit Award to the Gazan photojournalist, Motaz Azaiza, in collaboration with Trinity Boycott, Divestment & Sanctions (BDS). On Instagram, Law Soc highlighted his “courageous and uncompromising photojournalism”, noting “his images have documented not only devastation, but also resilience, dignity, and the enduring humanity of the people whose stories he tells”.
